title: Beyond Stoner-Wohlfarth: Machine-Learning Models and Symbolic Regression of Hard-Magnet Properties
authors: Samuel J. R. Holt, Christina Winkler, Timoteo Colnaghi, Martin Lang, Swapneel A. Pathak, Andrea Petrocchi, Michael Adams, Thomas Schrefl, Andreas Marek, Hans Fangohr
abstract: Predicting the extrinsic properties from hysteresis loops of a magnetic grain, namely the coercive field, remanent magnetisation, and maximum energy product, from its intrinsic micromagnetic parameters is a central problem in permanent-magnet modelling. Established analytical models provide useful estimates but often neglect nonuniform magnetisation processes, whereas direct micromagnetic simulations are computationally expensive. In this work, we train machine-learning models on 12012 micromagnetic simulations of an idealised cubic grain, spanning broad ranges of the saturation magnetisation, exchange constant, and uniaxial anisotropy constant. Benchmarked against the analytical models on identical held-out data, the machine-learning models predict all three extrinsic properties with substantially lower errors. Symbolic regression recovers the Kronmüller form of the coercive field, with an effective demagnetising factor that depends on the material, and finds new closed-form expressions for the remanence and maximum energy product. Each law contains at most two fitted constants yet approaches the accuracy of the machine-learning models. We also investigate the inverse problem of recovering the intrinsic parameters from the three extrinsic properties. The saturation magnetisation and anisotropy constant are recovered accurately, whereas the exchange constant is not, because it influences the extrinsic properties only weakly. The trained models are released through the mammos-ai Python package, enabling thousands of candidate parameter sets to be screened in seconds rather than the hours or days required by direct micromagnetic simulation.
summary: This work develops and validates machine learning models to predict key magnetic properties of hard magnets by analyzing data from extensive micromagnetic simulations. By combining ML with symbolic regression, the authors achieve high accuracy while drastically accelerating the prediction process compared to traditional physics simulations. This provides a powerful tool for materials discovery in magnetism.
main_problem: The central problem is predicting extrinsic magnetic properties (coercive field, remanence, maximum energy product) of hard magnets from their intrinsic micromagnetic parameters.
main_result: Machine learning models and symbolic regression significantly outperform established analytical models in predicting these properties with lower errors. The developed pipeline allows for rapid screening of candidate material parameters.
method: The study employs machine learning (Random Forest, Gaussian Process) trained on extensive micromagnetic simulations, supplemented by symbolic regression to derive closed-form physical laws.
model_or_system: The system is an idealized isolated cubic grain used to model magnetization reversal in hard magnets. The physics incorporates isotropic exchange, uniaxial anisotropy, and demagnetizing interactions within a micromagnetic framework.
key_observables: Coercive field (Hc), remanent magnetisation (Mr), maximum energy product (BHmax).
important_parameters: Saturation magnetisation (Ms), exchange constant (A), uniaxial anisotropy constant (K); the magnetic hardness parameter $\kappa = K / (\mu_0 M_s^2)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on micromagnetic simulations of an ideal, defect-free cubic grain and assumes that ML models can accurately map complex physical relationships.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between ML predictions and true values for intrinsic parameters (Ms, A, K) in the hard-magnet subset. Tables compare model errors (MAPE/RMSE) when performing the inverse problem (predicting intrinsic from extrinsic).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the prediction problem, details data generation via 12012 micromagnetic simulations across a broad parameter space, compares ML and symbolic regression against analytical models for all three properties, investigates the inverse problem, and concludes by releasing a fast predictive pipeline.
why_interesting: While focused on classical magnetism, the methodology—using advanced machine learning surrogates to bypass computationally expensive physics simulations—is highly relevant to modeling complex quantum many-body systems where direct simulation is intractable.
